svg.text: Ownership-First Default (Zero GC) • 12 Configurable Data Stack Policies (Manual or Compiler-Inferred) • Service-Isolated Arenas • Opt-In Manual & GC

g.text: Exit main() → Reclaims all Stacks & Heap
• Frame locals live on CPU stack
• Zero locks on service Data Stacks
All active Data Stacks & OS pages reclaimed
R1 Outlives Order: Stack A can point to
Stack B only if Lifetime(B) ≥ Lifetime(A).
R3 Service Boundary: Service Data Stacks
are private to its worker (Rule S1 & S8).
R4 HotPath Lock: Zero Data Stack growth
R5 Unified Backing: All 12 are policy
configs over core C arenas, slabs & indexes.
Heap — Container of Configured Data Stacks (12 Capability Policies)
Data Stacks are not separate rigid heaps—they are specialized storage configurations created manually by the developer or inferred by the compiler.
TIER 1: CORE MEMORY LAYOUTS & POOLS (EXISTING & EXPANDED)
• Zero padding, max L1 cache hit
• O(1) bulk wipe on scope exit
TIER 2: LIFECYCLE, VERSIONING, MULTI-SERVICE SHARING & STREAMING POLICIES
Delta CoW page allocated on update
TIER 3: QUERY INDEXING, ATOMIC TRANSACTIONS, SPATIAL & COMPRESSED POLICIES
Primary storage + automatically maintained secondary indexes
• Auto-updated on insert, controlled mutation, or delete
• Turns collections into embedded in-memory tables
• Distinct from Service (Service = access, Tx = consistency)
• Spatial: eliminates O(N²) collision & proximity scans
• Compressed: trades CPU decode for massive RAM savings
C Runtime Backing Layer: Typed Bump Arenas • Segregated Free-Lists • Segmented Slabs • Ring Buffers • Hash/BTree/Octree Indexes

svg.text: Architectural Principle: Data Stacks are composable storage policies, not 12 isolated heaps. Developers can configure them explicitly (e.g., DataStack<Indexed<Customer>>) or let the compiler select optimal policies automatically.
Hardware Scaling (fusion.toml): Scales from 4 KB on-demand pages with immediate OS release (Low Memory) to 2 MB Huge Pages with warm high-water retention (High Memory / HotPath).
